title: Speaking up about safety
place: Day 6 · 05:30 · off Port Everglades, main deck
goal: Speak up politely and clearly when something isn't safe, and report it.

l17-01.text: Bosun! Sorry, can I say something?

l17-02.text: Morning, cadet. Quick, I'm busy. What is it?
l17-02.es: Buen día, cadete. Rápido, que estoy ocupado. ¿Qué pasa?

l17-03.text: This grating is cracked. Look, here. The edge is up.
l17-03.es: Esta rejilla está rajada. Mirá, acá. El borde está levantado.

l17-04.text: Ah, yes. It's an old crack. It's OK, just walk around it.
l17-04.es: Ah, sí. Es una rajadura vieja. No pasa nada, pasá por al costado.

l17-05.text: Sorry, Bosun, but I don't think it's safe. It's a trip hazard. Someone could fall in the dark.
l17-05.es: Perdón, contramaestre, pero no creo que sea seguro. Es un peligro de tropiezo. Alguien se puede caer a oscuras.

l17-06.text: Hmm. You're right. At night nobody sees it.
l17-06.es: Mmm. Tenés razón. De noche nadie la ve.

l17-07.text: Can we put a barrier and a warning sign?
l17-07.es: ¿Podemos poner una barrera y un cartel de advertencia?

l17-08.text: Good idea. Bring the tape and a sign from the store. I'll stay here.
l17-08.es: Buena idea. Traé la cinta y un cartel del pañol. Yo me quedo acá.

l17-09.text: Here. Barrier tape and the sign.
l17-09.es: Acá está. Cinta de barrera y el cartel.

l17-10.text: Good. Now report it to the bridge. Say exactly where it is.
l17-10.es: Bien. Ahora reportalo al puente. Decí exactamente dónde está.

l17-11.text: Bridge, Diego. There's a cracked grating on the walkway between tank two and tank three, port side. We put a barrier and a sign. Over.
l17-11.es: Puente, Diego. Hay una rejilla rajada en la pasarela entre el tanque dos y el tres, babor. Pusimos una barrera y un cartel. Cambio.

l17-12.text: Received, Diego. Well done. Write a near miss report after the watch. Over.
l17-12.es: Recibido, Diego. Bien hecho. Escribí un reporte de casi accidente después de la guardia. Cambio.

l17-13.text: You see, cadet? Speaking up is part of the job.
l17-13.es: ¿Ves, cadete? Hablar es parte del trabajo.

screens.title: Where does NOT go?
steps: I don't think we should go this way.
paras: With think, English puts the not on think: I don't think + the rest positive. It sounds polite but clear.
To start: Sorry, can I say something? · Sorry to interrupt, but… · I'm worried about…
screens.avoid: I think it's not safe. · I think no. · I no think so.

screens.q: You think the ladder is dangerous. You say…
The bosun is busy, but you must tell him something. You start with…

screens.situation: The Second Officer wants to take a short cut over the cracked grating.
screens.q: Tell him.
What does Rolando think about the ladder?

screens.title: "Creo que no" → "I don't think so"
paras: Creo que no es seguro = I don't think it's safe. Creo que no (as an answer) = I don't think so.
And speaking up to a senior is normal and expected on board. It's part of the safety culture, not a lack of respect.
screens.avoid: I think that no. · I believe it's not safe.

screens.title: Polite, but firm
paras: Start soft: Sorry, Bosun…, with a rising, polite tone.
Then the important part goes down at the end, clear and calm: I don't think it's SAFE. A falling tone sounds sure. A rising tone sounds like a question.
